content.text: The comparison through day 1439 clarifies the remaining mismatches. The P14 water rate was 298 against a historical 602, the P16 water rate was 52 against 158, and P11 and P12 still produced too little water. I12-W began injecting water on day 1210. The simulated water saturation shows that the front on the static low-resistance path to P16 was still near the injector. The next round will test whether this connection is too weak, adjust inflow to the lower part of P14 and the arrival of water at P11 and P12, and continue to change only porosity and permeability.

Round 4 passed the original simulator's import checks. The 72267 active cells, well controls, temperature, initial pressure, and initial water saturation match, and the initial component sum has zero deviation in every cell. The full forward run has started. The baseline has reached day 2815, with 76 days left in the history.

I added a read-only tool to examine water-production contributions from individual completion cells. It uses the original wellbore gravity correction and well-to-cell flux equation. At the end of the baseline, the largest difference between the summed completion water rate and the original wellhead water rate across the six wells was about 0.006 m³/d. The check passed. These fluxes can help identify the intervals supplying water. The static paths remain leads for investigation.

The spatial results from round 4 show that the water front on the I12-W to P16 path has advanced toward the producer, while the rise in water production still lags the historical response. I will add a control that changes only porosity on this path, holding permeability and composition fixed, to test whether reducing storage volume can improve breakthrough timing. I will draw the conclusion after rerunning the entire history.

Over the common first 2119 days, round 4 further reduced field oil/water rate RMSE to about 346 m³/d, compared with 412 in round 3 and 1253 for the original fields. Individual-well errors improved at P11, P12, P14, P15, and P16. P13 performed worse than with the original fields, and late water production at P16 remains too low. I will retain these mismatches in the record and continue the full-period comparison.

Round 4 has also completed all 2891 days. Field oil-rate and water-rate RMSE each fell to about 721 m³/d. Combined NRMSE was 13.91%, and full-period error at all six wells was lower than with the original fields. The main remaining mismatch is the late water deficit at P16. Round 5 has passed 2380 days. Once it finishes, I will compare the full-period effect of changing only the porosity of the path.
